newsitem.title: INDIA: India Ranbaxy stresses value-added goods.
newsitem.headline: India Ranbaxy stresses value-added goods.

text.p: Indian pharmaceutical maker Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd said on Tuesday that a rise in domestic sales of value-added "dosage-form" products in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) more than offset a sharp drop in bulk drug sales.

Ranbaxy said in a statement that domestic sales of dosage-form products such as tablets grew 19 percent during the six months ended September 30, while sales of bulk drugs -- which are inputs to make shelf medicines-- fell 66 percent.
Overall domestic sales grew 11 percent to 2.67 billion rupees compared with the same period in 1995.
Exports surged 41 percent to 2.45 billion rupees, pushing total first-half sales to 5.12 billion rupees, up 23 percent over the first half of 1995, it said.
The statement quoted chairman Parvinder Singh as telling a board meeting that "the emergent environment demanded an emphasis on value addition".
"In India, the focus in the past few months has been on competitive repositioning and on moving towards higher value-added products as a response to an increasingly vibrant market," it said.
A company official, asked to explain the high rate of sales growth in the export market, said price controls within India encouraged foreign sales.
The statement said net profit was 718 million rupees in the first half of 1996/97, up from 595 million in the same period in 1995/96.
Gross profit was 963 million rupees, up from 798 million.
Depreciation was 135 million, up from 107 million.
Profit before tax amounted to 828 million rupees, up from 691 million, while the provision for taxation rose to 110 million from 96 million.
